entries.progress_note: PDF text/OCR parsing now supports bounded 1/2/4-worker page chunks with deterministic page-order merge; full format and 10GB coverage remain planned.

Concurrent documents remain isolated. A FAILED PermissionError now receives exactly one post-batch isolated retry; all other failure classes remain explicit and are not retried automatically. Broader ingest-format completion remains planned.

Native PDF pages retain a deterministic page type, specification section/Part/clause locators, and bounded table rows with bboxes. Drawing pages now accept only one explicit native-text Sheet value in a bounded title-block region; callouts, unlabeled codes, vision narration and conflicts fail closed. Detectable vector drawing tables retain exact per-cell offsets and bboxes, and explicit legacy five-digit Sections are preserved without accepting arbitrary five-digit values. Canonical retrieval keeps same-table sibling rows bounded to one run/document/page/table and intersects different exact identifier types along one structural path. A generic-name multi-page PDF carries the latest exact digit-bearing RFI/Submittal identifier, role and status through ordered continuation pages until another exact heading replaces it; 1/2/4-worker output remains equivalent without another PDF scan. Text-layer slicing, word coordinates, local OCR fallback and bounded timeout checkpoints remain. Borderless/cross-page tables, multi-column reading order and complete semantic coverage remain planned; see docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md.

DOCX body paragraphs and table text retain native element and line locators. Exact RFI/Submittal identifier, role and status changes now split one table into separate evidence fragments while workflow state continues across body elements. Complete heading, list, merged-table, image, header/footer, revision and comment structure remains planned.

Local OCR, EXIF normalization, PDF CropBox coordinate transforms, selective overview routing, one bounded high-resolution schedule-table crop, evidence schema and matching previews are implemented. General drawing-region crops and live crop-quality validation remain planned.

RFC-style EML and bounded local Outlook MSG share one safe evidence path. Each MIME alternative group selects one non-empty body, preferring plain text then safe HTML; conflicting same-type choices warn instead of merging. A multipart/related start selects its matching Content-ID, with the first child as the standards fallback; non-root resources stay inert. EML and MSG parser inventory plus selected import use one MIME-derived name for unnamed parts so supported resources stay analyzable. Only a Subject with a normalized digit-bearing workflow ID can outrank an exact body heading. Allowlisted same-line metadata is separated from its exact ID; status values must be complete apart from terminal punctuation, so keyword-prefixed prose stays neutral. Every distinct exact marker is retained; a body-routed primary stops at any different exact RFI/Submittal section, while established valid-Subject priority remains. Exact Gmail, Yahoo, Proton and Outlook HTML boundaries keep history outside current routing and extraction. Thread headers accept bounded angle-bracketed local@domain tokens only. Every nested message MIME part stays inert. python-oxmsg handles MSG; mailbox sync, attachment recursion and semantic thread inference remain planned.

Exact RFI/Submittal aliases and workflow labels normalize across selected Email body, valid Subject and filename into a bounded index. Same-line metadata stays outside IDs; complete known statuses remain neutral metadata without precedence. Cross-scope references cannot donate role/status; malformed threads and inert resources cannot manufacture roles. Hash-only threads, selected attachments and SQLite projection stay model-free. Terminal-run pages reuse one bounded process-local index; active runs stay fresh, and a versioned/audited classification correction invalidates the cache while immutable Email provenance remains visible.

Customer-configured Autodesk APS and Procore bearer connections browse and selectively import remote documents without remote writes. Imports reuse project limits, chunks, hashes and deduplication; live tenant validation and interactive OAuth remain planned.

A reviewer can inspect bounded attachment metadata and explicitly import one attachment or a batch of up to 100 selected EML or MSG attachments. A batch parses the parent once and prevalidates every index/SHA-256 before upload creation, then reuses capacity, chunk, hash and deduplication controls. Nested messages and non-root resources remain inert. Immutable parsed-Email metadata keeps explicit attachment provenance visible after a run-scoped RFI/Submittal/Other correction. No analysis or model call starts automatically.

Explicit RFI roles, complete Submittal statuses and EML source roles are preserved before extraction; exact PDF scope persists across continuation pages. A reviewer can apply/reset a versioned current-run RFI/Submittal/Other overlay; it invalidates the terminal index without mutating evidence, candidates or Email provenance. Full semantic classification and other dimensions remain planned.

Mixed valid and ineligible workflow citations are filtered per evidence ID: RFI questions, rejected Submittals, email headers and quoted history cannot remain as direct material or QA support. Full revision-scope comparison remains planned.

Candidate conditions now inspect every remaining direct source, so a later RFI response, Submittal or current email body cannot be hidden by an earlier specification citation. A single Submittal source with multiple distinct explicit statuses is marked ambiguous instead of selecting one. Full cross-document latest-value selection remains planned.
A deterministic pre-publication check rejects descriptor/generic material names and removes duplicate or evidence-misaligned properties. Full option/entity mapping remains planned.

Mixed-source requirement and property citations are pruned per evidence ID while a field with valid direct support is preserved. Complete field-level evidence coverage across every output remains planned.

A deterministic QA check requires an executable inspection/test action, excludes non-QA documents and generic objects, and keeps full extraction evidence for review. Full QA type coverage remains planned.

The local dashboard shows a stage-weighted analysis percentage, an elapsed-time estimated finish, coverage and aggregate timing. Persisted page summaries now derive a visual status from their visual-task states. Polling is serialized and active runs avoid full result loading; the complete production dashboard remains planned.
D-27 implements user-selectable 1/2/4 local document parsing workers. Paid API requests remain serial; broader queued task orchestration is still planned.

D-27 adds aggregate stage, provider-wait, and model-response metrics plus processed-page counts. Per-call export and retry summaries remain planned.

Adjacent eligible extraction batches are capped at four fragments/8.8 KB with a stable recovery family. Ordinary evidence and matching exact workflow scopes still batch, while different RFI identifiers or roles, Submittal identifiers or statuses, and RFI/Submittal families close the batch before one prompt. Email headers, recognized history and signatures close locally. A single PDF uses bounded page chunks whose ordered merge carries exact workflow scope identically for 1/2/4 workers without another PDF scan. A concurrent document PermissionError receives one isolated local retry after its batch; paid calls remain serial and broader distributed orchestration remains planned.

The English main application has a dedicated Model API Settings section and every open tab now detects a completed same-port restart before retaining stale provider controls. The API key field remains write-only and explicitly accepts a new or replacement key. The existing gateway, budget, active-work block and Windows current-user DPAPI boundaries remain unchanged; offline replacement-key tests make no model call.

Workflow-classification corrections record actor, time, run/document target, before/after values and reviewer note in append-only events. Complete upload, analysis, export and deletion audit coverage remains planned.

DEV-173 adds schema-only candidate isolation with atomic source-linked issues, blocked historical snapshots and shared server/UI resume eligibility. Customer runtime is unchanged; current acceptance: docs/AUDIT_REMAINING_VALIDATION.md. A complete production retry queue is still not implemented.

DEV-173 adds safe publication issue identifiers/contract paths and indexed task-family metadata lookup without copying whole-run response bodies. Current validation: docs/AUDIT_REMAINING_VALIDATION.md. Complete production observability remains planned.

Native PDF evidence now carries detected Section, Part, clause, and bordered table-row context. Deterministic property checks reject context citations from a different document or non-local evidence range. Full inherited definitions, exceptions, footnotes and cross-page tables remain planned.

Selective routing still limits vision to large-format, low-text graphic, or dense-graphic pages. Detected specification/schedule tables now use one bounded high-resolution crop with full-page coordinates, stable region identity, cache separation and crop preview; other eligible pages retain one overview call. General drawing-region detection and live crop-quality validation remain planned.
The live setup checks the target application port before loading, saving, forgetting or forwarding a credential, and reports the conflict without stopping the existing process.

Project questions automatically use the newest saved terminal project analysis. Retrieval now keeps bounded native same-page siblings, uses a retained visual Sheet locator only as a native-page routing hint, and preserves multiple distant matches in one long fragment. Explicitly requested structured arithmetic is locally recomputed from cited non-date/non-identifier operands; conversions, date math, rounding and geometry inference remain blocked. Terminal answer failures retain only a stable safe diagnostic category.

Bounded native page siblings and multi-window fragments repair split context; visual Sheet labels route only to native page evidence. Explicit arithmetic uses a structured contract and local exact recomputation. Terminal failures keep a stable safe reason code.
The project knowledge endpoint selects the newest saved PARTIAL or COMPLETED run, reports active/stale state without evidence text, and lets the browser ask without an Analysis Run selection.

The no-provider legacy-versus-QA-V2 retrieval comparison script and synthetic structural-table regression are implemented. The workspace's fixed customer benchmark databases remain under .local and were not read by this task; no authorized external staging snapshot was available, so the release thresholds, browser cutover and legacy general-retrieval deletion remain unclaimed.
